messages.author: 1ee26a82d11c44a1
messages.subject: Bootstrap with DWLS estimator
parts:
Dear scientists,

I used DWLS estimator for my model because the data is non-normal. As far as I know, the DWLS can be used with non-normal data, but the same is not true for ML estimator. My inquiry is: is it necessary to use both DWLS estimator and bootstrap to deal with non-normal data? My code is: 

fit <- cfa(model,sample.nobs = 758, data=M,estimator = "DWLS", standadized=TRUE,se = "bootstrap")

It yielded the same estimates but different standard error with the command without the argument "se = "bootstrap"":

fit <- cfa(model,sample.nobs = 758, data=M,estimator = "DWLS", standadized=TRUE)

Thank you very much for reading my question.

Best regards,

Tran Viet Yen.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Bootstrap with DWLS estimator
parts: As far as I know, the DWLS can be used with non-normal data
Specifically, it is for binary or ordinal outcomes, not continuous non-normal data.
but the same is not true for ML estimator
For continuous non-normal data, you can use robust ML.  See the description of the estimator, se, and test arguments in the ?lavOptions help page.
My inquiry is: is it necessary to use both DWLS estimator and bootstrap to deal with non-normal data?

No.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
